name: Taxes
description: Fiscal categories and per-jurisdiction tax rules, plus the engine that resolves the rate at sale time.

agent.description: Manages fiscal categories (the linkable tax_category_key), per-jurisdiction tax rules (the % by country+region+category, with multi-tax components like surcharge), and category aliases for CSV import. Resolves the applicable tax for a sale line by category.

ai.description: Lists the canonical fiscal categories (the linkable tax_category_key)
Gets a fiscal category by its canonical key (FK validation for import)

Lists all tax rules (rate + fiscal qualification by country+region+category, including multi-tax components). The qualification says whether the operation is subject, exempt or not subject, under which regime, and — when exempt — the exemption cause. `is_incoherent` = 1 marks a rule with a rate on a class that charges no tax (its own class, or its root's, is not subject): sales under it cannot be invoiced until it is repaired with `taxes.rules.repair` — filter with is_incoherent=1 to find them.
Lists tax rules for a given country
Lists category aliases (external text → canonical key) used by CSV import
Resolves an external alias text to a canonical tax_category_key

Configuration state of the tax module: how many active, currently valid root tax rules match the hub's fiscal country. Zero means the sale engine cannot resolve a rate for what this hub sells, so the till would fall back to a guessed one.
Creates a fiscal category with a canonical key

expect_rows.message: That rule could not be created: a reverse-charge, exempt or not-subject rule charges no tax, so its rate must be 0 and no component with a rate can hang from it; a component must hang from a root rule of this business with the same country, region and tax category; and its validity range cannot run backwards.

ai.description: Creates a tax rule (the % for a country+region+category) with its fiscal qualification (operation_class / regime_key / exempt_reason). Any operation_class other than subject (reverse charge, exempt, not subject) charges no tax, so its rate_pct must be 0. Pass parent_id to add a multi-tax component (e.g. surcharge) to a root rule of class subject.

Creates multiple tax rules at once (e.g. 'create the 2026 Spain VAT rates'). Invalid rows (including a non-subject operation_class with rate_pct > 0) are skipped without aborting the batch. Components (parent_id) must be created individually.
Deactivates a tax rule so it no longer applies to new transactions (issued invoices keep their snapshot)

expect_rows.message: That rule could not be brought back: it does not exist in this business, or it is already active.

ai.description: Brings a deactivated tax rule back so it applies to new transactions again (undoes `taxes.rules.deactivate`). Its rate, jurisdiction, category, validity and components are untouched — deactivating never changed them.

expect_rows.message: That rule could not be repaired: it does not exist in this business, or it has nothing to repair — only a rule that charges no tax (reverse charge, exempt, not subject) but still carries a rate, or a component with a rate under such a rule, can be repaired.

ai.description: Repairs ONE incoherent tax rule (is_incoherent = 1 in taxes.rules.list): a rule that charges no tax (reverse charge, exempt, not subject) saved with a rate, or a component with a rate under such a root. Sales of that category are charged at the till but cannot be invoiced until it is repaired. mode 'no_tax' (default) sets the rate to 0 (and clears the rates of the root's components); mode 'charge_tax' keeps the rate and makes the rule subject (drops the exemption reason). Ask the owner which one they meant before calling it. Past sales and issued invoices are not changed.
Persists a category alias (external text → canonical key) learned during CSV import
Resolves and calculates the applicable tax for an amount by fiscal category (country/region from the hub's fiscal identity), returning the rate AND the fiscal qualification of the operation
